shortAnswer: Per-release list of behavior changes from Android 13 through 17, plus what each forces you to do.
Use it to quote target-API dates or to plan an audit with the SDK Upgrade Assistant.
items.answer:
What changed per release, and what it forces you to do. Verified 2026-08-07.

#### Android 13 (API 33)
- **`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission.** Notifications are opt-in. Request it in context, not on first launch.
- **Granular media permissions** — `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` / `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO` / `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO` replace `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`.
- Themed app icons; per-app language preferences.
- Nearby Wi-Fi devices permission split out of location.

#### Android 14 (API 34)
- **`foregroundServiceType` is mandatory** — declare it and hold the matching permission, or you crash on start. Play reviews the declared type.
- **Implicit intents to internal components blocked** — an intent aimed at your own non-exported component must be explicit.
- **Partial media access** — `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED`. The user can grant access to *specific* photos, so 'granted' is no longer binary.
- Runtime-registered receivers must declare `RECEIVER_EXPORTED` / `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`.
- Non-dismissable notifications can be dismissed by the user.

#### Android 15 (API 35)
- **Edge-to-edge by default** for apps targeting 35. Handle `WindowInsets` properly or your content sits under the system bars.
- Foreground service restrictions tightened further; `dataSync` and `mediaProcessing` get timeouts.
- Predictive back is on by default for apps that opted in.
- 16 KB page size support becomes relevant for apps targeting 15+.

#### Android 16 (API 36) — current stable
- **Edge-to-edge enforcement broadens**; the opt-out APIs are deprecated for apps targeting 36.
- Adaptive/large-screen behaviour changes: apps are expected to handle resizing rather than lock orientation.
- Predictive back further standardized.

#### Android 17 — released
- **Local network access blocked by default** for apps targeting 17. New `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` permission; guidance is to prefer privacy-preserving pickers over scanning the LAN.
- **Background audio restrictions** — the audio framework enforces while-in-use rules for foreground services, with alarm-audio exemptions, gated on `targetSdk`.

#### Play policy dates — memorize these two
| Date | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **2026-08-31** | New apps and updates must target **API 36**. Existing listings must target ≥ API 35. Extension available to **2026-11-01**. |
| **2027-02-01** | Updates without **16 KB page size** support can no longer be released. |

#### How to audit your app
1. Android Studio → **SDK Upgrade Assistant** — lists the behavior changes that affect your code per API level.
2. Use the **compatibility framework** toggles (Developer Options → App Compatibility Changes) to enable individual `targetSdk`-gated changes *before* bumping `targetSdk`.
3. For 16 KB: check for bundled `.so` files (including transitive dependencies) and verify ELF alignment.

items.q: Gradle, AGP & R8 flags quick reference
shortAnswer: Flag-by-flag reference for `gradle.properties`, configuration cache, `--scan`, and diagnosing slow builds.
Covers AGP 9, KSP versus kapt, R8 full mode with keep rules, and App Bundle splits.
Use it for build-speed questions, release hygiene, or version-catalog and `implementation` versus `api`.
items.answer:
The flags worth knowing by heart, and what each actually buys. Verified 2026-08-07.

#### gradle.properties — build speed
- `org.gradle.parallel=true` — build independent modules concurrently
- `org.gradle.caching=true` — reuse task outputs across builds
- `org.gradle.configuration-cache=true` — skip the configuration phase entirely
- `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g -XX:+UseParallelGC`
- `android.nonTransitiveRClass=true` — a resource change doesn't recompile the world
- `kotlin.incremental=true`
The configuration cache is usually the single biggest win on a large project. It requires build logic that doesn't read mutable state at execution time.

#### Diagnosing
- `./gradlew assembleDebug --profile --scan` — where time actually goes
- `./gradlew :app:dependencies` — resolve a version conflict
- `./gradlew --stop` — kill stale daemons
Read the build scan before optimizing anything. The bottleneck is rarely where you assume.

#### AGP 9.x (current: 9.3.0, Jul 2026)
- **Kotlin is applied by the Android plugin itself** — remove `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` from module scripts.
- AGP 9.0 (Jan 2026) was the breaking migration; use the **AGP Upgrade Assistant** in Android Studio.
- KMP projects with Android targets needed a specific migration for AGP 9.

#### KSP vs kapt
`plugins { alias(libs.plugins.ksp) }` and `dependencies { ksp(libs.room.compiler) }` — not `kapt`.
kapt generates Java stubs for every Kotlin file — very expensive. KSP reads Kotlin directly, typically ~2x faster. One remaining kapt processor holds the whole module back, so finishing the migration matters more than it looks.

#### Release build — R8
`release { isMinifyEnabled = true; isShrinkResources = true; proguardFiles(getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"), "proguard-rules.pro") }`
R8 does shrinking, optimization, obfuscation, and desugaring in one pass. **Full mode** is more aggressive and can break reflection — always test the minified release build, and archive `mapping.txt` per release or your crash reports are unreadable.

Common keep rules:
- `-keepclassmembers,allowobfuscation class * { @com.google.gson.annotations.SerializedName <fields>; }`
- `-keepclasseswithmembernames class * { native <methods>; }`

#### App Bundle splits
`bundle { language { enableSplit = true }; density { enableSplit = true }; abi { enableSplit = true } }`
Usually the largest single size saving — users download only what their device needs.

#### Version catalog — `gradle/libs.versions.toml`
- `[versions] kotlin = "2.4.10"`, `agp = "9.3.0"`, `composeBom = "2026.06.01"`
- `[libraries] compose-bom = { group = "androidx.compose", name = "compose-bom", version.ref = "composeBom" }`
- `[plugins] android-application = { id = "com.android.application", version.ref = "agp" }`

#### Dependency hygiene
Prefer `implementation` over `api` — `api` leaks onto consumers' compile classpath and widens the recompilation blast radius. Use `api` only when a type genuinely appears in your module's public signatures.

#### Useful checks
- `./gradlew lint` — Android lint
- `./gradlew detekt ktlintCheck` — static analysis / formatting
- `./gradlew :app:bundleRelease` — produce the AAB
